property_summary: After a successful fallback call with 9 ether (bug) vs 10 ether (reference), the reference does not trigger the balance transfer while the bug does, causing address(c).balance to be 9 ether in the reference and 0 in the bug version.

After a first call sending 10 ether at a timestamp > 0, at a block number where block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract's balance becomes 0 (due to transfer of all balance), but the buggy contract (requiring 9 ether) did not accept the 10 ether and thus reverts, leaving its balance unchanged.

After a call to fallback with exactly 9 ether, the modified contract accepts the call while the reference requires 10 ether, so the reference reverts and the modified one succeeds, allowing a subsequent withdrawal via the if(block.number % 15 == 0) branch.

After a successful fallback call with 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the contract's balance becomes 0 when block.number % 15 == 0; the buggy version requires 9 ether so it reverts on the first call, leaving the balance unchanged.

After two calls to fallback with a 15-block interval (block.number % 15 == 0 on the second call), the reference requires block.timestamp > pastBlockTime and thus reverts on a reentrant call within the same second, whereas the buggy version allows it and transfers the balance out, causing address(c).balance to be 0 ether instead of the reference's 20 ether.
Two identical calls to fallback at blocks where block.number % 15 != 0 succeed when timestamps are equal, but reference accepts only strictly increasing timestamps while bug version accepts >=.

After a first call to fallback() at block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance becomes 0. The second call with the same timestamp (via vm.warp) reverts in the reference because block.timestamp must be > pastBlockTime, but succeeds in the buggy version where >= is allowed, thus breaking the invariant that only strictly increasing timestamps are accepted.

After a fallback call with 10 ether at block number 15, the reference reverts if a second call occurs at the same timestamp (block.timestamp == pastBlockTime), but the modified version accepts it, making a subsequent call at block.number%15==0 transfer the entire balance to the caller.

Calling fallback with 10 ether twice in the same block when block.number % 15 == 0: reference reverts second call (require block.timestamp > pastBlockTime), but buggy version allows it and sends balance to sender twice.

After two calls to fallback with 10 ether each at blocks where block.number % 15 == 0 (first call) and block.number % 15 != 0 (second call), the reference contract transfers the entire balance to the caller on the first call and nothing on the second, so the contract balance is 0; the buggy version transfers on the second call instead, leaving balance 10 ether.
After a single call with exactly 10 ether when block.number % 15 == 0, the reference version sends the balance to the caller while the buggy version does not (condition flipped).

Send 10 ether twice: reference transfers balance on block numbers divisible by 15, bug transfers on non-divisible blocks, causing observable divergence in contract balance after second call at block number where first call triggers transfer and second does not.

After sending 10 ether in a block where block.number % 15 == 0, the reference version transfers the entire contract balance to the sender, while the bug version (using !=) does not, leaving the balance unchanged.

When the block number is 15 (so block.number % 15 == 0), the reference version sends the contract balance to the caller, while the buggy version (with !=) does not, making the contract balance different after the call.
Two calls: first sends 10 ether after warp(1) which passes, second sends 10 ether after next block (warp(2) + vm.roll(target+1)) — reference succeeds, second version reverts due to final revert().

After a successful fallback call that meets the require conditions and transfers balance in block % 15 == 0, the reference contract remains active for further calls while the modified version always reverts, making a second call fail.

After a successful fallback call transferring 10 ether, the reference contract retains the balance (if block.number % 15 != 0), while the second version always reverts after updating pastBlockTime, so address(c).balance remains unchanged, causing a divergence when checking the balance after a call.
